    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.IsometryMatrices.Basic, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Matrices preserving a Gram matrix #

    For a square matrix A over a commutative semiring, Matrix.isometryMatrices A is the submonoid of matrices X with Xᵀ * A * X = A, the endomorphisms of the coordinate module that preserve the bilinear form with Gram matrix A. Counting these matrices over the finite rings ZMod (p ^ r) is how the local density of a quadratic lattice is defined, and the two results here are what that count needs.

    • A change of basis A ↦ Pᵀ * A * P by an invertible P conjugates the submonoid by P, so its cardinality does not depend on the basis. Neither does it change under reindexing or under a ring isomorphism of the coefficients.
    • Let f : R →+* S be surjective with square-zero kernel, let 2 be a unit of R, and let A be symmetric with unit determinant. Then every solution over S lifts to a solution over R, and the solutions over R lying above a fixed one correspond to the skew-symmetric matrices with entries in the kernel. Hence, as an identity of Nat.cards, the count over R is Nat.card (ker f) ^ (k.choose 2) times the count over S, for k the size of the index type; when R is finite these are the actual numbers of solutions. This is the infinitesimal lifting property behind the smoothness of the orthogonal group of a nondegenerate form away from 2, with its relative dimension k (k - 1) / 2.

    The lift corrects an arbitrary preimage M of the solution: with error E = A - Mᵀ * A * M, the matrix M * (1 + ½ A⁻¹ E) is a solution, since all quadratic terms in the error vanish.

    Main results #

    • Matrix.natCard_isometryMatrices_transpose_mul_mul: the count is invariant under A ↦ Pᵀ * A * P for invertible P.
    • Matrix.natCard_isometryMatrices_reindex, Matrix.natCard_isometryMatrices_map_ringEquiv: the count is invariant under reindexing and under ring isomorphisms.
    • Matrix.exists_map_eq_of_mem_isometryMatrices_map: solutions lift across a surjection with square-zero kernel.
    • Matrix.isometryMatricesFiberEquiv: the solutions congruent to a given one modulo a square-zero ideal correspond to the skew-symmetric matrices with entries in the ideal.
    • Matrix.natCard_isometryMatrices_eq_pow_mul: the count across such a surjection.

    References #

    • C. L. Siegel, Über die analytische Theorie der quadratischen Formen, Ann. of Math. 36 (1935), where the local densities are defined by these counts.

      theorem Matrix.add_transpose_mul_mul_add_of_sq_eq_bot {n : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [CommRing R] {I : Ideal R} (hI : I ^ 2 = ⊥) {A X D : Matrix n n R} (hA : A.transpose = A) (hX : X ∈ A.isometryMatrices) (hD : ∀ (i j : n), D i j ∈ I) :
      (X + D).transpose * A * (X + D) = A + X.transpose * A * D + (X.transpose * A * D).transpose

      The square-zero expansion of the isometry equation. If X preserves a symmetric Gram matrix A and the entries of D lie in a square-zero ideal, then the quadratic term of (X + D)ᵀ * A * (X + D) vanishes, leaving A + K + Kᵀ for K = Xᵀ * A * D.

      noncomputable def Matrix.isometryMatricesFiberEquiv {n : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [CommRing R] {I : Ideal R} (hI : I ^ 2 = ⊥) {A X₀ : Matrix n n R} (hA : A.transpose = A) (hdet : IsUnit A.det) (hX₀ : X₀ ∈ A.isometryMatrices) :
      { X : ↥A.isometryMatrices // ∀ (i j : n), ↑X i j - X₀ i j ∈ I } ≃ { K : Matrix n n R // (∀ (i j : n), K i j ∈ I) ∧ K.transpose = -K }

      The solutions congruent to a given one modulo a square-zero ideal form a torsor under the skew-symmetric matrices with entries in the ideal. Let A be symmetric with unit determinant and let X₀ preserve A. The solutions X with X - X₀ having entries in a square-zero ideal I correspond to the skew-symmetric K with entries in I, via K = X₀ᵀ * A * (X - X₀) and X = X₀ + (X₀ᵀ * A)⁻¹ * K.
